1173585598080344064.a: My mother hosted foreign exchange students from Saudi Arabia. Both Shia and Sunni.

1173585599032377344.a: The Shia students never left their room, prayed nearly all day every day, and spent hours a day screaming on the phone at people. They were very inwardly focused. School and Prayer, little else. They made people nervous somehow even if they didn't intend to.

1173585600378810368.a: The Sunni students were the exact opposite, outgoing, carefree, hanging out at the Hookah bar watching the belly dancers, cooking big community meals in our kitchen, buying American muscle cars on a whim. What you might expect out of the Middle Eastern youth.

1173585601700016134.a: The Shia students seemed to treat the Sunnis as reckless and Godless and only gave the Sunni angry stares. The Sunni students mumbled "Terrorist" at the Shia students as they crossed paths. They refused to speak more than single word.

1173585603465814016.a: The actual conflict is not something we are likely ever going to understand. And, really, is it our place to understand it? I'm not sure. They definitely need to sort it out on their own, though. And we need to just step back and feed and care for them both until they do.

1173585604862500864.a: Why should we step back? Because, like it or not, we have this same conflict in the US and we don't even recognize it. All these mass shootings and bomb mailings are the same old story. We need to deal with our own story before we tell other people what their story should be.
